It is stated that in respect of the accident the police of PS Sarojini Nagar had registered an FIR No. 355/2013 u/s 279/337 IPC.
It is averred that the petitioner had received grievous and multiple injuries on various parts of his body as per his medical documents.
It is averred that the petitioner remained under complete bed rest for about four months and under treatment for a long period and spent a huge amount on his treatment.
He was still taking medicines and feeling pain in his injured leg.
It is averred that the petitioner was aged about 63 years and was working as a salesman/ supplier of various daily needs products and was earning Rs.10,000/ per month approximately.
It is averred that the accident was caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by the respondent No.1.

It is averred that the respondent No.1 is the driver and owner of the vehicle and the respondent No.2 is the insurance company of the offending vehicle and as such all the respondents are jointly, severally and vicariously liable for the payment of compensation.
It is prayed that an amount of Rs.10,00,000/ be awarded as compensation in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents.

3. Reply was filed on behalf of the respondent No.1 taking the preliminary objections that the claim calculated by the petitioner is baseless having no truth in it and the same has been filed only to harass the respondent No.1 and to extort money from the respondent No.1.
It is averred that the complainant is concealing the material and true facts from the Court and has come before the Court with unclean hands.
It is stated that on 17.10.2013 the driver namely Mr. Ramesh Chand of the respondent No.1 was driving the car and the respondent No.1 was sitting on the back seat of the car.
It is stated that the car bearing No.DL2C AL 6799 (Maruti Alto) is fully insured by the National Insurance Company Ltd.
It is averred that the record and the complaint made by the claimant while recording of the FIR are contradictory and shows that the respondent No.1 has been falsely implicated in the case.

It is stated that the statement of the complainant in the FIR states that a male driver was driving the vehicle and was accompanied by a lady while in the statement of the respondent No.1 forcibly recorded by the police official in the notice under section 133 of M.V Act it is stated that the respondent No.1 was driving the vehicle on the day of accident.
The averments made in the claim petition were denied.
It is averred that the petitioner is a senior citizen and may have suffered from other ailments also.

4. Reply was filed on behalf of the National Insurance Company Ltd. stating that the policy bearing No.35101031126132325672 valid from 08.12.2012 to 07.12.2013 in the name of Smt. Asha Saxena was issued by the company for vehicle No.DL2CAL6799.

It is averred that the learners license No.DL12/LL/8886/1314 dated 23.09.2013 in the name of Ms. Asha Saxena W/o Shri Pradeep Kumar Saxena for motorcycle without gear/ LMV (NT) only was found genuine as per verification report filed by the police.

My findings on the specific issues are as under:
12.

As the petition has been filed U/s 166 M.V Act it was incumbent upon the petitioner to prove that he sustained injuries in an accident caused due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.

To determine the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle it has been held in National Insurance Company Ltd. vs Pushpa Rana & Another 2009 Accident Claims Journal 287 as follows:
"The last contention of the appellant insurance company is that the respondents/claimants should have proved negligence on the part of the driver and in this regard the counsel has placed reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. V. Meena Variyal (supra).

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. V. Meena Variyal
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On perusal of the award of the Tribunal, it becomes clear that the wife of the deceased had produced: (i) certified copy of the criminal record of criminal case in FIR No.955 of 2004, pertaining to involvement of offending vehicle (ii) criminal record showing completion of investigation of police and issue of charge sheet under sections 279/304A, Indian Penal Code against the driver; (iii) certified copy of FIR, wherein criminal case against the driver was lodged; and (iv) recovery memo and mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle and vehicle of deceased.
These documents are sufficient proofs to reach the conclusion that the driver was negligent.
Proceedings under the Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to proceedings in a civil suit and hence strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.
Hence, this contention of the counsel for the appellant also falls face down.
There is ample evidence on record to prove negligence on part of the driver."

It is established law that in a claim petition under Motor Vehicle Act, the standard of proof to establish rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle is not at par with the criminal case where such rashness and negligence is required to be proved beyond all shadow of reasonable doubt.

In Kaushnamma Begum and others v. New India Assurance Company Limited, it was inter alia held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that the issue of wrongful act or omission on the part of the driver of the motor vehicle involved in the accident has been left to a secondary importance and mere use or involvement of motor vehicle in causing bodily injury or death to a human being or damage to property would make the petition maintainable under Sections 166 and 140 of the Motor Vehicle Act.

18. It is significant that R1W1 admitted that the IO had issued a notice under Section 133 M.V. Act and a perusal of the same shows that the respondent No.1 had stated thereon that she was driving the vehicle at the time of the accident.

The respondent No.1 had tried to contend that her statement was forcibly recorded by the police official in the notice under section 133 of M.V Act to state that the respondent No.1 was driving the vehicle on the day of the accident.

However there is nothing to show that the respondent No.1 had made any complaint to any higher authority that her statement was got forcibly recorded by the police official in the notice under section 133 of MV Act and it was on her own statement that the respondent No.1 was arrested in the present case.

A perusal of the charge sheet shows that initially the matter was sent as untraced and thereafter an application was moved by the nephew of the injured wherein he had stated that in the MLC the name of the person who had admitted the injured was stated as Asha Saxena.
The MLC also shows that the name of Asha Saxena is mentioned therein.

Thereafter the nephew of the injured had traced the address of the respondent No.1 and further proceedings were undertaken and she was given notice under Section 133 MV Act on which she had stated that she was driving the offending vehicle at the time of the accident.

19. PW1 was crossexamined on coming to Delhi on the day of the accident and belonging to Bulandshahar but nothing much turns on the same.
As far as the manner of the accident is concerned PW1 stated that the offending vehicle was being driven at high speed.
He denied the suggestion that the offending vehicle had turned from the red light and came towards him.
It is not in dispute that the offending vehicle had hit the petitioner and it was stated that the offending vehicle was not being driven rashly and negligently.
However it is clear that the driver of the offending vehicle was unable to control the vehicle and hit the petitioner.
The criminal record has been placed on record which shows that the respondent No.1 has been charge sheeted for the offence under Sections 279/338 IPC.

In Basant Kaur and others v. Chattar Pal Singh and others 2003 ACJ 369 MP (DB) it was observed that registration of criminal case against the driver of the offending vehicle was enough to record a finding that the driver of the offending vehicle was responsible for causing the accident.

sentences.text: There is nothing to disprove the involvement of vehicle No.DL2CAL6799 in the accident.
In view of the testimony of PW1 and the documents on record which have remained unrebutted, the negligence of the respondent No.1 has been prima facie proved.
At the same time the petitioner was also negligent in crossing the road and the same is corroborated by the site plan prepared by the IO.

A perusal of the site plan shows that there is nothing to indicate a zebra crossing at the spot of the accident or to show any spot for crossing and quite clearly the petitioner was not crossing the road from any spot meant for crossing the road.

The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in Koosappa Poojari v. K. Sadabba & Ors. MFA No.6208 of 2002 decided on 21.11.2003 observed that the driver of the vehicle ought to have been more prudent and circumspect while driving.

entities.text: Koosappa Poojari v. K. Sadabba & Ors. MFA No.6208 of 2002
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It was however also observed:
"But it cannot be lost sight of the fact that a duty is also cast on a pedestrian and he should use due care and caution in going upon and crossing the road and it is his duty to look out for on coming traffic.

In so far as the another duty cast on the pedestrian is concerned, it is needless to say that he has to give the driver a plenty of time to see him and slow down and start before he attempts to cross or put one foot on the crossing.
It is not always necessary that the vehicular traffic will have to stop for a pedestrian to cross, for the vehicle needs more time to stop in view of the speed a motor generates.

Moreover, whenever a pedestrian is crossing over a roadway at any place other than which is meant for pedestrian crossing, they cannot claim any specific precedence and the responsibility for causing the accident more often than not will have to be shared by the pedestrian along with the vehicle driver.
In view of this, it cannot be said that it was only the driver of the vehicle in question was solely responsible for the accident."

"The following observation of the High Court of Australia in Astley v. Austrust Ltd.
((1999) 73 ALJR 403) is worthy of quoting.
A finding of contributory negligence turns on a factual investigation whether the plaintiff contributed to his or her own loss by failing to take reasonable care of his or her person or property.
What is reasonable care depends on the circumstances of the case.
In many cases, it may be proper for a plaintiff to rely on the defendant to perform its duty.
But there is no absolute rule.
The duties and responsibilities of the defendant are a variable factor in determining whether contributory negligence exists and, if so, to what degree.

In some cases, the nature of the duty owed may exculpate the plaintiff from a claim of contributory negligence; in other cases, the nature of the duty may reduce the plaintiff's share of responsibility for the damage suffered; and in yet other cases the nature of the duty may not prevent a finding that the plaintiff failed to take reasonable care for the safety of his or her person or property.

The duty owed by the defendant, although relevant, is one only of many factors that must be weighed in determining whether the plaintiff has so conducted itself that it failed to take reasonable care for the safety of its person or property."

Although the petitioner has not filed any document on record in order to prove the expenditure on conveyance however, notice can be taken of the fact that after the accident the petitioner was taken to AIIMS and thereafter to Safdarjung Hospital and that after discharge from hospital he might have hired the services of private conveyance as he would not have been able to drive of his own or to use public conveyance.
Shri Bundi vs Smt Asha Saxena on 11 February, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51047985/
14 APPORTIONMENT OF LIABILITY:
It is the case of the respondent No. 2 that the respondent No.1 was not in possession of a valid and effective driving license on the date of the accident which amounted to a fundamental breach of the condition of the policy.
Thus it is the case of the respondent No.2 that the respondent No.1 was in possession of a learner license at the time of the accident which was in violation of the MV Rules.
35.
36. A perusal of the insurance policy shows that it contains a clause that a person holding an effective learner's license may also drive the vehicle and that such a person satisfies the requirements of Rule 3 of the Central Motor Vehicle Rules, 1989.
Even the learner's license of the respondent No.1 clearly refers to the provisions of Rule Shri Bundi vs Smt Asha Saxena on 11 February, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51047985/
15 (3) of the CMV Rules,1989 and that the same prohibits her from driving any motor vehicle unless she has besides her a person duly licensed to drive the vehicle and in every case, the vehicle carries "L" plates both in the front and in the rear of the vehicle.
The respondent No.1 was accompanied by Shri Ramesh Chand who was a person duly licensed to drive the vehicle at the time of the accident.
As such there is nothing on record to absolve the respondent No.2 - insurance company of its liability to pay the compensation amount.

This issue is decided accordingly.
37. In view of the above discussion the respondents No.1 and 2 are held jointly and severally liable.
The respondent No.2 i.e. The National Insurance Co. Ltd. had in its reply stated the policy bearing No. 35101031126132325672 valid from 08.12.2012 to 07.12.2013 in the name of Smt. Asha Saxena was issued by the company for vehicle No.DL2CAL6799.
Hence, the respondent No.2 being the insurance company in respect of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation on behalf of the respondent No.1.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer is directed to deposit the award amount in the court by way of crossed cheque/ demand draft within 30 days of the passing of the award with interest at the rate of 9% from the date of filing of the DAR till its realization failing which it is liable to pay interest at the rate of 12% per annum for the period of delay.
38. Nazir to report in case the cheque is not deposited within 30 days of the passing of the award/judgment.
Nazir is directed to note the particulars of the award amount in the register today itself.
The petitioner shall file his complete address as well as address of his counsel for sending the notice of deposit of the award amount.
The insurer shall deposit the award amount along with interest upto the date of notice of deposit to the claimant with a copy to his counsel and the compliance report shall be filed in the court along with proof of deposit of award amount, the notice of deposit and the calculation of interest on 12.5.2015.
An attested copy of the award be given to the parties (free of cost).
File be consigned to record room.
